hypothesis: Reading the next MoE layer's predicted experts ahead (the router applied early to the residual) shortens the stalls the in-layer overlap leaves.
model: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD, all 70 layers, native MXFP4 experts and FP8/BF16 dense
command:
git checkout 845474fc
c/build_mimo_cuda.bat
mingw32-make -C c mimo CUDA_DLL=1 ARCH=native VK=0
python c/tools/benchmark_mimo_cuda.py --engine c/mimo.exe --model D:/AI/Models/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD --shards C:/AI/MiMoPro-Shards --backend cuda --release-host --cap 104 --threads 16 --read-threads 16 --context 16384 --tokens 64 --runs 3 --env MIMO_PREFETCH=0|1 --output <dir>

hardware.ram: 192 GiB installed (4 x 48 GiB), DDR5 configured at 5400 MT/s; 191.08 GiB OS-visible; ~65 GB/s measured read bandwidth
hardware.storage: C: one PCIe 5.0 x4 NVMe (88 shards, ~10.5 GB/s direct 19 MB reads); D: three PCIe 4.0 NVMe striped behind the chipset (42 shards, ~6.5 GB/s); ~17.7 GB/s together. Native Windows unbuffered reads.
hardware.os: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 10.0.26300; MinGW-w64 GCC 14.2 MSVCRT, MSVC 14.44; RTX 4090 24 GiB WDDM, driver 617.42, CUDA Toolkit 13.2, sm_89

quality.method: All measured 64-token greedy replies byte-identical to the release engine's (reply SHA-256 0305abcd...); tiny-oracle logits byte-identical to the pre-change engine; full 70-layer CPU/CUDA logit gate in correctness/.
